title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Texas Stock Exchange LLC; Notice of Filing, and Order Granting Accelerated Approval of, a Proposed Rule Change To Amend Rule 17.111(d) (Commodity-Based Trust Shares)
raw_text:
Self-Regulatory Organizations; Texas Stock Exchange LLC; Notice of Filing, and Order Granting Accelerated Approval of, a Proposed Rule Change To Amend Rule 17.111(d) (Commodity-Based Trust Shares)

1. Purpose TXSE Rule 17.111(d) currently governs the listing and trading of Commodity-Based Trust Shares on the Exchange. Under the existing rule, the Exchange is required to submit a separate proposed rule change pursuant to Section 19(b) of the Act before listing Commodity-Based Trust Shares. The Exchange proposes to amend Rule 17.111(d) to establish generic listing standards that would permit the Exchange to list and trade Commodity-Based Trust Shares that satisfy the requirements of Rule 17.111(d) pursuant to Rule 19b-4(e) under the Act. Commodity-Based Trust Shares that do not satisfy the applicable generic listing standards could continue to be listed pursuant to a separate proposed rule change under Section 19(b) of the Act. Background The proposed standards are substantially similar to generic listing standards previously approved by the Commission for Nasdaq, Cboe BZX, and NYSE Arca. In July 2026, the Commission approved amendments to Nasdaq's generic listing standards that, among other things, permit up to 15% of the net asset value (``NAV'') of a Trust's holdings to consist of certain digital commodities and securities that do not otherwise satisfy the applicable generic eligibility criteria, add a definition of ``digital commodity,'' and permit actively managed Commodity-Based Trust Shares, subject to additional safeguards. The Commission subsequently approved substantially similar amendments for NYSE Arca and Cboe BZX and materially identical amendments for Nasdaq Texas. The Exchange's proposal incorporates both the original generic listing standards and the subsequent amendments into Rule 17.111(d), with changes necessary to conform the Exchange's existing rule structure, definitions, and cross-references. Proposal The Exchange proposes to amend Rule 17.111(d) to permit the Exchange to list and trade Commodity-Based Trust Shares that satisfy the requirements of Rule 17.111(d) pursuant to Rule 19b-4(e) under the Act. Rule 19b-4(e) provides that the listing and trading of a new derivative securities product by a self-regulatory organization is not deemed a proposed rule change pursuant to Rule 19b-4(c)(1) if the Commission has approved, pursuant to Section 19(b) of the Act, the self-regulatory organization's trading rules, procedures, and listing standards for the product class that would include the new derivative securities product and the self-regulatory organization has a surveillance program for the product class. Consistent with the Commission-approved generic listing standards, the Exchange would retain the ability to submit a proposed rule change pursuant to Section 19(b) of the Act to list and trade Commodity-Based Trust Shares that do not satisfy one or more of the applicable generic listing standards. The proposed rule would also provide that statements or representations contained in any such proposed rule change concerning (1) the description of the index, Trust holdings, or reference assets; (2) limitations on the index, Trust holdings, or reference assets; (3) the dissemination and availability of the index, Trust holdings, reference assets, or Intraday Indicative Values; or (4) the applicability of Exchange listing rules would constitute continued listing requirements. An issuer would be required to notify the Exchange of any failure to comply with such continued listing requirements. If the Commodity-Based Trust Shares do not satisfy those requirements, the Exchange may suspend trading and will initiate delisting proceedings under the TXSE Rule Series 16.500. Definitions The Exchange also proposes to modernize the definition of Commodity-Based Trust Shares in renumbered Rule 17.111(d)(3). As proposed, Commodity-Based Trust Shares could be issued by a trust, limited liability company, partnership, or other similar entity that, if applicable, is operated by a registered commodity pool operator pursuant to the Commodity Exchange Act and is not registered as an investment company under the Investment Company Act of 1940, or a series or class thereof. Consistent with its stated investment objective and policies, a Trust could hold one or more commodities or commodity-based assets and, in addition, securities, cash and cash equivalents. The proposed rule would also retain the existing creation and redemption structure, as expanded to accommodate the broader range of permitted holdings and cash creations and redemptions based on the next determined NAV per Trust share. The Exchange also proposes to amend the definition of ``commodity'' in Rule 17.111(d)(3)(B) to provide that the term is defined in Section 1a(9) of the Commodity Exchange Act and does not include an ``excluded commodity'' as defined in Section 1a(19) of the Commodity Exchange Act. Proposed Rule 17.111(d)(3)(C) would define the term ``commodity- based asset'' as any future, option, or swap on a commodity, as defined in proposed Rule 17.111(d)(3)(B). Proposed Rule 17.111(d)(3)(D) would define the term ``digital commodity'' as a commodity that is a digital asset and is intrinsically linked to and derives its value from the programmatic operation of a functional crypto system, as well as supply and demand dynamics, rather than from the expectation of profits from the essential managerial efforts of others. Proposed Rule 17.111(d)(3)(E) would define the term ``cash equivalent'' as a short-term instrument with a maturity of less than three months consisting of: (1) U.S. Government securities, including bills, notes, and bonds differing as to maturity and rates of interest, that are either issued or guaranteed by the U.S. Treasury or by U.S. Government agencies or instrumentalities; (2) certificates of deposit issued against funds deposited in a bank or savings and loan association; (3) bankers' acceptances; (4) repurchase agreements and reverse repurchase agreements; (5) bank time deposits; (6) commercial paper; and (7) money market funds. title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; Nasdaq Texas, LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposal To Amend Equity 4, Rule 4120, To Align It With That of The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC
raw_text:
Self-Regulatory Organizations; Nasdaq Texas, LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposal To Amend Equity 4, Rule 4120, To Align It With That of The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC

1. Purpose When in September of this year the Exchange updated its rulebook at Equity 1 and Equity 4 to more closely align those rules with the equivalent rules of The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC (``Nasdaq''), in anticipation of the Exchange becoming a primary listing venue in 2027, the Exchange mistakenly copied an obsolete version of Nasdaq Equity 4, Rule 4120. The Commission had approved the current version of Nasdaq Equity 4, Rule 4120, back in 2022. However, this version of the rule did not become operative until August of this year. This delay in making the 2022 changes operative on Nasdaq led to the Exchange mistakenly copying in its September 2026 filing an obsolete version of Nasdaq Equity 4, Rule 4120. The Exchange proposes to correct this mistake in this filing. The Exchange proposes to replace in its entirety its current version of Equity 4, Rule 4120, with the version of that rule that is currently found in the Nasdaq rulebook. Therefore, the new version of Nasdaq Texas Equity 4, Rule 4120, would be structured as follows: 1. Section (a) (Definitions) defines certain terms that are used in the rule. 2. Section (b) (Regulatory Halts) establishes the Exchange's authority to initiate regulatory halts or pauses in various circumstances, including: halts provided for by the applicable SIP Plan; discretionary Regulatory Halts relating to issuer information, material news, initial public offerings, index warrants, derivative securities products, foreign securities, market disruptions, and Initial ETP Opens; and mandatory Regulatory Halts relating to dissemination issues for derivative securities products, the Limit Up- Limit Down Mechanism, market-wide circuit breakers, Equity Investment Tracking Stocks and Subscription Receipts, and reverse stock splits. 3. Section (c) (Operational Halts) establishes the Exchange's authority and procedures for initiating and terminating Operational Halts, including: the circumstances in which Nasdaq Texas may declare an Operational Halt, notification to the SIP when Nasdaq Texas has concerns about collecting and transmitting quotation or transaction information or has declared an Operational Halt or suspension, and the procedures for resuming trading when Nasdaq Texas determines that trading may resume in a fair and orderly manner. The changes that the Exchange would make to the Nasdaq rule to tailor it to the Exchange would be the following: 1. Modify references to the operating hours and trading sessions of the Exchange, so that they correctly reflect those of Nasdaq Texas. This includes not carrying over language in Nasdaq Equity 4, Rule 4120, that pertains to Nasdaq's upcoming transition to trading 23 hours a day, 5 days a week. 2. Eliminate references to a direct listing with capital raise, as that option is not present in the Nasdaq Texas rulebook. 3. Update references to ``Nasdaq'' with ``Nasdaq Texas.'' Additionally, the Exchange will not copy references to the CORE FIX order entry protocol that are currently present in Nasdaq Equity 4, Rule 4120. This is because the Exchange, Nasdaq, and Nasdaq PHLX LLC will be imminently submitting separate filings to abandon their plans to deploy the CORE FIX order entry protocol, due to a lack of interest by exchange participants. Therefore, it makes no sense for the Exchange to copy references to CORE FIX in Nasdaq Equity 4, Rule 4120, that will soon become obsolete. 2. Statutory Basis The Exchange believes that its proposal is consistent with Section 6(b) of the Act, in general, and furthers the objectives of Section 6(b)(5) of the Act, in particular, in that it is designed to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system, and, in general to protect investors and the public interest. The Exchange believes that the proposed rule change will remove impediments to, and perfect the mechanism of, a free and open market and a national market system by aligning the Exchange's rulebook at Equity 4, Rule 4120, with the substantially similar rule of Nasdaq, which was previously approved by the Commission, finding it to be consistent with the Act. The proposal is also consistent with Section 6(b)(5) because it is designed to promote clarity, consistency, and transparency for Participants, issuers, and market participants by replacing stale rule text with the version of Equity 4, Rule 4120, that reflects the Commission-approved Nasdaq framework and the intervening updates already incorporated into Nasdaq's current operative rule. The Commission previously approved Nasdaq's Rule 4120 framework to add categories of regulatory and operational halts, reorganize Rule 4120, incorporate provisions of the applicable equity data plans, and make conforming changes to related rules. In approving that framework, the Commission recognized that the revisions promote a clear and uniform approach to trading halts, improve coordination and certainty among plan participants and market participants, enhance the resiliency and integrity of market systems, and promote fair and orderly markets and investor protection. Nasdaq Texas's proposal advances those same objectives because it would adopt a substantially similar halt framework while tailoring only the exchange name, trading session terminology, and other conforming elements needed to reflect the Exchange's existing rules and operations. The Exchange therefore believes the proposal will reduce confusion, support consistent cross- market halt and resumption procedures, and help Participants understand when the Exchange may halt, pause, or resume trading and how related rules will operate. title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; New York Stock Exchange LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of Proposed Rule Change To Amend Exchange Rule 2(c)
raw_text:
Self-Regulatory Organizations; New York Stock Exchange LLC; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of Proposed Rule Change To Amend Exchange Rule 2(c)

1. Purpose The Exchange proposes to amend Rule 2 (``Member,'' ``Membership,'' ``Member Firm,'' etc.) to restore language inadvertently omitted from the proposed definition of ``associated person'' in a recent rule filing. More specifically, the proposed change is a technical amendment that would ensure that the persons encompassed by the ``approved person'' category that the Exchange recently filed to delete are captured by the definition of ``associated person'' in Rule 2(c) for jurisdictional and all other applicable Exchange rules. The proposed rule change is not intended to effect any substantive change to the scope of the Exchange's jurisdiction. Background and Proposed Rule Change On September 18, 2026, the Exchange filed an immediately effective rule change to (1) eliminate the ``approved person'' registration category as no longer necessary, (2) adopt a new definition of ``associated person'' in Rule 2(c) based on the definition of associated person in Rule 1011(b) of the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority, Inc. (``FINRA'') and elements of the current definition of approved person, and (3) make related technical and conforming changes. The Approved Person Filing is scheduled to become operative on October 18, 2026. As described in the Approved Person Filing, the Exchange did not intend to expand or narrow the scope of its jurisdiction. Rather, the proposal was designed to ensure that all persons currently encompassed by the approved person category would continue to be covered under the proposed definition of ``associated person.'' Specifically, the filing stated that proposed Rule 2(c)(3) would include the existing categories of approved persons: (i) persons that control a member organization; (ii) persons engaged in a securities or kindred business that is controlled by a member or member organization; and (iii) U.S. registered broker-dealers under common control with a member organization. The filing further explained that the proposed definition of ``Control Person'' was intended to encompass those same categories. The Exchange has since determined that the text of proposed Rule 2(c)(3), as filed, inadvertently omitted the clause covering persons engaged in a securities or kindred business that is controlled by a member or member organization. That clause appears in the Exchange's current approved person definition and was intended to be carried forward without substantive change. Consequently, the text of proposed Rule 2(c)(3) is inconsistent with both the description of the proposal and the Exchange's stated intent in the Approved Person Filing, which was to preserve, rather than modify, the existing scope of Exchange jurisdiction. This proposed rule change corrects that inadvertent omission and conforms the rule text to the proposal as described in the Approved Person Filing. The Exchange accordingly proposes to amend Rule 2(c)(3) to add the phrase ``a person engaged in a securities or kindred business that is controlled by a member or member organization,'' immediately after ``controlled by a member organization,''. As amended, Rule 2(c)(3) would provide that an associated person includes: (3) any person (excluding a governmental entity) directly or indirectly controlling or controlled by a member organization, a person engaged in a securities or kindred business that is controlled by a member or member organization, or a U.S. registered broker-dealer under common control with a member organization (a ``Control Person''). No other changes are proposed to Rule 2. The Exchange proposes that this proposed rule change become operative on the same date as the Approved Person Filing, and therefore requests that the Commission waive the 30-day operative delay so that this proposed rule change may become operative concurrently with the Approved Person Filing and ensure that the rule text accurately reflects the proposal as originally described before the Approved Person Filing takes effect. 2. Statutory Basis The Exchange believes that the proposed rule change is consistent with Section 6(b)(5) of the Act, in that it is designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices, to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to foster cooperation and coordination with persons engaged in facilitating transactions in securities, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest. In particular, the Exchange believes that the proposed technical correction would remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system by ensuring that the text of Rule 2(c) accurately reflects the categories of persons described in the Approved Person Filing, which are the categories the Exchange has treated as within its jurisdiction under the current approved person definition. Restoring the omitted clause would eliminate potential ambiguity as to whether persons engaged in a securities or kindred business controlled by a member or member organization are Control Persons and associated persons under Exchange rules. The Exchange believes this clarity would preserve its ability to exercise jurisdiction over those persons and would thereby protect investors and the public interest. The Exchange further believes that the proposed change is consistent with the Act because it does not alter the approach described in the Approved Person Filing of defining associated person by reference to FINRA Rule 1011(b) and the definition of associated person of a broker or dealer in Section 3(a)(18) of the Act. The proposed change would simply conform the rule text to the scope of the proposal as described in that filing. B. title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; NYSE Arca, Inc.; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of Proposed Rule Change To List Shares of the Bitwise 10 Crypto Index ETF Under NYSE Arca Rule 8.201-E (Generic)

Self-Regulatory Organizations; NYSE Arca, Inc.; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of Proposed Rule Change To List Shares of the Bitwise 10 Crypto Index ETF Under NYSE Arca Rule 8.201-E (Generic)

1. Purpose The Exchange proposes to change the manner in which the shares of the Fund (``Shares'') are listed and traded on the Exchange. The Shares were originally approved to list and trade on the Exchange pursuant to Rule 8.500-E. The Exchange now proposes to list and trade Shares of the Fund on the Exchange pursuant to Rule 8.201-E (Generic). The Commission approved the listing and trading of shares of the Fund (the ``Shares'') on the Exchange under Rule 8.500-E on July 22, 2025. Rule 8.500-E governs the listing and trading of Trust Units, which are securities issued by a trust, limited liability company, or other similar entity that, if applicable, is constituted as a commodity pool and that holds investments comprising or otherwise based on any combination of futures contracts, options on futures contracts, forward contracts, swap contracts, commodities, and/or securities. On July 28, 2026, the Commission approved a proposed rule change to amend Rule 8.201-E (Generic). Rule 8.201-E (Generic), as amended, allows for up to 15% of a trust's net asset value (NAV) to consist of digital commodities or securities that do not independently meet the core generic eligibility criteria; adds ``digital commodity'' as a defined term; and allows for actively managed Commodity-Based Trust Shares. The Exchange proposes to now list and trade the Shares of the Fund pursuant to the generic listing standards set forth in Rule 8.201-E (Generic), as amended, which would permit the Fund to operate in reliance on the generic listing standards in Rule 8.201-E (Generic), as amended, instead of the terms of the Original Approval Order. The Exchange represents that the Shares will meet the requirements of Rule 8.201-E (Generic), as amended, on an initial and continued listing basis. In addition, the Exchange will comply with the requirements of Rule 19b-4(e) to list and trade Shares of the Fund on the Exchange. 2. Statutory Basis The Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act and the rules and regulations thereunder applicable to the Exchange and, in particular, the requirements of Section 6(b) of the Act. Specifically, the Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Section 6(b)(5) requirements that the rules of an exchange be designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices, to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to foster cooperation and coordination with persons engaged in regulating, clearing, settling, processing information with respect to, and facilitating transactions in securities, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system, and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest. The Exchange believes the proposed rule change is designed to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest because it would allow the Fund to be listed and traded under Rule 8.201-E (Generic), as amended, instead of Rule 8.500-E. The proposed change would permit the Fund to operate in reliance on the generic listing standards in Rule 8.201-E (Generic), as amended, instead of the terms of the Original Approval Order, thereby facilitating the listing and trading of an exchange-traded product that will enhance competition among market participants, to the benefit of investors and the marketplace. The Exchange represents that the Shares will meet the requirements of Rule 8.201-E (Generic), as amended, on an initial and continued listing basis. B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purpose of the Act. As discussed above, the proposed change is intended to facilitate the initial and continued listing and trading of the Shares on the Exchange, thereby promoting competition among exchange-traded products to the benefit of investors and the marketplace. C. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others No written comments were solicited or received with respect to the proposed rule change. III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action The Exchange has filed the proposed rule change pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A)(iii) of the Act and Rule 19b-4(f)(6) thereunder. Because the proposed rule change does not: (i) significantly affect the protection of investors or the public interest; (ii) impose any significant burden on competition; and (iii) become operative prior to 30 days from the date on which it was filed, or such shorter time as the Commission may designate, if consistent with the protection of investors and the public interest, the proposed rule change has become effective pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A) of the Act and Rule 19b- 4(f)(6)(iii) thereunder. A proposed rule change filed under Rule 19b-4(f)(6) normally does not become operative prior to 30 days after the date of the filing. However, pursuant to Rule 19b-4(f)(6)(iii), the Commission may designate a shorter time if such action is consistent with the protection of investors and the public interest. At any time within 60 days of the filing of such proposed rule change, the Commission summarily may temporarily suspend such rule change if it appears to the Commission that such action is necessary or appropriate in the public interest, for the protection of investors, or otherwise in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. If the Commission takes such action, the Commission shall institute proceedings under Section 19(b)(2)(B) of the Act to determine whether the proposed rule change should be approved or disapproved. News CategoryAlertMarketsWhat You Need To Know
Data Technical News#2026-025The Nasdaq Stock Market

On October 15, 2026, the shareholders of Supernus Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (SUPN) approved the proposed merger with and into a subsidiary of Indivior Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (INDV). As a result of the merger, Supernus Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (SUPN) will be suspended from Nasdaq and Indivior Pharmaceuticals, Inc. will have a name and symbol change to Supernus, Inc., using the symbol SUPN previously used by Supernus Pharmaceuticals, Inc., effective November 3, 2026.

Nasdaq requests that market data redistributors note this is a symbol reuse and history should NOT carry over from the current SUPN to the new SUPN effective Tuesday, November 3, 2026. The history from INDV should carry over to SUPN effective November 3, 2026.
